newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei surges to close nearly 500 points up.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei surges to close nearly 500 points up.

text.p: Tokyo stocks surged upwards on Wednesday, with the key index ending up nearly 500 points at its highest close in four months.

The rally was inspired by a surge on Wall Street on Tuesday and the yen's weak trend against the dollar. Plans by a number of firms to buy back their own shares, announced in recent weeks, also brightened the market, brokers said.
The Nikkei average of 225 leading shares ended up 480.75 points or 2.57 percent at 19,151.12. A few minutes before the close it had opened up a 500-point gap from Monday's close.
Nikkei June futures added 600 to close at 19,250.
The market was closed on Tuesday for a holiday.

Shares in Mitsubishi Chemical Corp, a leading Japanese chemical company, jumped 20 yen to end at 427, after it announced on Monday that it plans to buy back up to 40 billion yen worth of its own stock, or up to 100 million shares. Its trading volume of 6.099 million shares was the fourth-heaviest on the first section of the Tokyo bourse.
Last week, Toyota Motor Corp said it had decided to buy back up to 100 billion yen worth of its own shares. The major automaker's shares jumped 110 yen to 3,680.
An early rally in stocks was inspired by Tuesday's upturn on Wall Street, brokers said.
On Tuesday, the Dow industrials closed up 179 points or 2.65 percent at 6,962, as weaker-than-expected U.S. economic data soothed Wall Street's concerns over rising interest rates.
"The U.S. stocks' surge has erased one unclear factor that Tokyo has worried about," said Seiki Orimi, manager of stock information services at Dai-Ichi Securities Co Ltd.
There had been fears in Tokyo that strong U.S. economic data might hit the Dow this week and that any sharp decline could damage Japanese stocks, brokers said.
But many participants were still cautious, waiting to see if the Fed's policy-setting meeting raises rates next month.

"Selling-back pressure was firm at around 19,229.49 (an intra-day high marked on February 24) and the Nikkei's rise fizzled short of that level. The next focus is whether it will be able to breach that point tomorrow," said a broker at a medium-sized local securities house.
On the first section of the Tokyo bourse, turnover was 458 million shares on Wednesday, up sharply from Monday's 257 million. Japanese markets were closed on Tuesday for a holiday.
Winning issues overwhelmed losers 1,011 to 142, while 88 issues were unchanged.
In other indices, the broader TOPIX index rose 30.34 points or 2.15 percent to close at 1,441.19, and the Nikkei 300 average rallied 6.04 points or 2.21 percent to 279.75.
By sector, fisheries, warehousing, air transport, brokerages and banks led the advancers. There were no major declining sectors.
The recent stabilisation of the yen at a low level against the dollar encouraged buying of blue-chip high-technology issues.
Shares in Canon Inc rose 40 yen to end at 3,010, while Sony Corp jumped 100 yen to end at 9,240.

Shiseido Co Ltd shares hit a high for this calendar year of 1,850 yen, after it announced on Monday that it had agreed to buy one of Helene Curtis Industries Inc's HC.N Japanese units. Shiseido ended 60 yen higher at 1,820.
In Osaka, Tateho Chemical Industries Co Ltd ended at a daily limit low of 279 yen, hurt by Monday's announcement that its liabilities exceeded its assets on a group basis.
The second section index gained 12.93 points to 1,667.00, with 7.35 million shares traded. The over-the-counter (OTC) index was up 8.62 points at 1,143.18 in late trade.
-- Hiroko Nakata, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-8027
